title: Novel Algorithms — 10 True Innovations
brief: 10 genuinely new algorithms not found in any existing PRISM engine: clothoid blending, wear-pattern refinishing, PH curves, multi-body vibration, thermal field toolpath, minimum-jerk trajectory, Voronoi-medial-axis pocketing, stochastic toolpath routing, inverse thermal compensation, contact-mechanics surface integrity.

units.title: ClothoidBlendingEngine — G2-continuous Euler spiral transitions
units.description: Implement clothoid/Euler spiral blending for toolpath corners. Curvature varies linearly with arc length: κ(s) = s/A². Use Fresnel integrals C(t)=∫cos(πu²/2)du, S(t)=∫sin(πu²/2)du for XY coordinates. Taylor series approximation (5 terms sufficient for <0.1μm error). Replaces quadratic Bezier corner rounding with G2-continuous transitions that eliminate jerk at blend boundaries. Methods: blendCorners(path, min_radius), computeClothoid(L, A), fresnelIntegral(t). Material: 6 materials from existing thermal DB.
exit_conditions: Clothoid geometry computed via Fresnel integrals
G2 continuity verified (curvature continuous at junctions)

units.title: PHCurveToolpathEngine — Pythagorean-Hodograph exact arc-length
units.description: Implement PH quintic curves per Farouki (2008). Property: x'(t)² + y'(t)² = σ(t)² where σ is a polynomial — exact arc length in closed form. Build PH quintic Hermite interpolant from endpoint positions and tangents. Exact feed rate = ds/dt without approximation. Methods: phQuinticInterpolate(p0, t0, p1, t1), exactArcLength(t0, t1), constantFeedParameterization(targetFeed). Eliminates feed approximation errors in constant-speed machining.
exit_conditions: Exact arc length verified against numerical integration

units.title: VoronoiMedialAxisPocketEngine — Mathematically optimal pocketing
units.description: Implement Voronoi diagram of pocket boundary → medial axis → offset pocketing. Fortune's sweep-line O(n log n) for Voronoi construction. Extract medial axis as Voronoi edges interior to pocket. Generate toolpath by offsetting from medial axis at variable distance to maintain constant engagement angle θ = arccos(1-ae/R). Methods: computeVoronoi(boundary), extractMedialAxis(voronoi, boundary), generateOffsetPath(medialAxis, toolDiameter, targetEngagement). Superior to heuristic spiral patterns.
exit_conditions: Voronoi diagram computed from pocket boundary

units.title: MinimumJerkTrajectoryEngine — Smoothest possible CNC motion
units.description: Implement minimum-jerk trajectory per Flash & Hogan (1985). Minimize ∫j²dt via 5th-order polynomial segments: x(t) = a0 + a1*t + a2*t² + a3*t³ + a4*t⁴ + a5*t⁵ with boundary conditions on position, velocity, acceleration. Solve 6x6 linear system per segment. Produces smoother motion than trapezoidal or S-curve profiles. Methods: minimumJerkSegment(x0, v0, a0, xf, vf, af, T), planTrajectory(waypoints, maxVel, maxAccel), computeJerkProfile(trajectory).
exit_conditions: Jerk is minimized (verified by comparison with S-curve)

units.title: WearPatternRefinishEngine — Spatial wear compensation
units.description: TRUE GAP: No system compensates for spatial wear variation. Map non-uniform VB(z) along cutting edge → predict surface error profile e(z) = f(VB(z), forces, geometry) → generate compensating finish pass with offset = -e(z). Uses AdvancedWearPhysicsEngine flank VB ODE output as input. Interpolate VB along edge from discrete measurements. Methods: mapWearProfile(vb_measurements), predictSurfaceError(wearProfile, forces, geometry), generateCompensatingPass(errorProfile, originalPath), estimateLifeExtension(wearProfile).

Surface error predicted from wear pattern
Tool life extension quantified (1-2 extra finish passes)

units.title: MultiBodyVibrationEngine — Coupled tool-holder-workpiece dynamics
units.description: Model tool + holder + spindle + workpiece + fixture as coupled mass-spring-damper system. Transfer matrix method: [M]{ẍ} + [C]{ẋ} + [K]{x} = {F(t)}. Assemble system from component FRFs (Frequency Response Functions). Predict system natural frequencies and mode shapes. Identify coupled chatter modes invisible to single-body analysis. Methods: assembleSystem(components), computeSystemFRF(freq_range), predictCoupledModes(), stabilityLobesCoupled(rpm_range, depths). Uses receptance coupling substructure analysis (RCSA).
exit_conditions: Coupled stability lobes differ from single-body

units.title: ThermalFieldToolpathEngine — 2D transient thermal field routing
units.description: Solve 2D transient heat equation ∂T/∂t = α∇²T + Q̇ on coarse grid (32×32) via explicit finite difference. Track cumulative thermal field as toolpath progresses. Route toolpath to avoid heat accumulation zones (T > threshold → skip zone, return later when cooled). Extends TGAR (point estimates) to full 2D field tracking. Methods: initializeGrid(workpiece_dims), applyHeatSource(x, y, Q, dt), stepTimeForward(dt), findCoolZones(threshold), routeToolpath(zones, strategy).
exit_conditions: 2D heat equation solved via finite difference
Temperature field evolves correctly over time
Hot zones avoided during toolpath routing

units.title: ContactMechanicsSurfaceEngine — Hertz contact + sub-surface integrity
units.description: Hertz contact stress at tool-workpiece interface: p_max = (6*F*E*²/(π³*R²))^(1/3). Sub-surface von Mises stress field: σ_VM(z) from Huber solution. Predict plastic zone depth where σ_VM > yield. White layer risk when temperature exceeds austenite threshold. Residual stress sign from mechanical (compressive) vs thermal (tensile) contributions. Methods: hertzContact(F, R, E_star), subSurfaceStress(p_max, a, z), plasticZoneDepth(stressField, yield), whiteLaverRisk(Vc, feed, material), residualStressSign(mechanical, thermal).
exit_conditions: Sub-surface stress field matches analytical solution

units.title: StochasticToolpathRoutingEngine — Monte Carlo strategy optimization
units.description: Treat toolpath strategy selection as stochastic optimization. Sample N=100 toolpath variants by perturbing: entry point (random boundary point), cut direction (±15°), step pattern (zigzag/spiral/contour), engagement (±20%). Evaluate each with Kienzle force, Taylor tool life, cycle time. Build Pareto front (time vs quality vs life). Select by user priority or return full Pareto set. Methods: sampleVariants(pocket, N, perturbation_ranges), evaluateVariant(variant, material, tool), buildParetoFront(evaluations), selectOptimal(pareto, priority).
exit_conditions: Each evaluated with Kienzle + Taylor physics

units.title: InverseThermalCompensationEngine — Real-time machine thermal correction
units.description: Combine MachineToolErrorBudgetEngine thermal model with EnvironmentalVariationEngine to compute inverse compensation field. Predict thermal growth at each axis position: δ(x,y,z) = Σ αᵢ × ΔTᵢ × Lᵢ for each error source. Apply inverse offset: corrected = nominal - δ. Support real-time updating from temperature sensor inputs. Methods: predictThermalField(machine, temperatures, run_time), computeCompensation(thermalField, toolPosition), applyCompensation(blocks, compensationField), updateFromSensors(sensorReadings).
exit_conditions: Thermal field predicted from machine model + environment
